title: How to Grill Thinly Sliced Eggplant for Vegan Sandwiches
meta_description: Learn how to grill eggplant slices on mat for the perfect vegan sandwich. Get tips on slicing, seasoning, and avoiding the dreaded eggplant stick.
html:
Eggplant is a superstar in vegan cooking, but it can be a nightmare on the grill. If you've ever tried to cook thin slices, you know the struggle: they either slide right through the grill grates or stick so stubbornly that you tear the vegetable apart trying to flip it. The secret to getting those perfect, gold-brown marks without the mess is to grill eggplant slices on mat.

By using a non-stick barrier, you can achieve a tender, smoky texture that holds up beautifully in a sandwich without the risk of flare-ups. Here is exactly how to master this process for your next plant-based feast.

Choosing and Prepping Your Eggplant

For sandwiches, I recommend the Italian globe eggplant. It has a meaty texture and a consistent shape that makes slicing easier. Look for a firm eggplant with a shiny, deep purple skin; if it feels soft or looks dull, it's likely overripe and will be too spongy.

The key to a great sandwich slice is thickness. Aim for about 1/4 to 1/2 inch. Any thinner and they might disintegrate; any thicker and the outside burns before the middle softens. Use a sharp chef's knife to cut the eggplant lengthwise into ovals. This shape fits much better on a standard loaf of sourdough or ciabatta than round circles do.

To reduce bitterness and prevent the eggplant from absorbing too much oil, sprinkle the slices with salt and let them sit for 20 minutes. Pat them dry with a paper towel before seasoning. This simple step ensures a firmer texture and a better sear.

The Best Way to Grill Eggplant Slices on Mat

When you're ready to hit the heat, preheat your grill to medium-high. Instead of placing the vegetables directly on the grates, lay down your BBQ Grill Mats. This creates a stable, non-stick surface that prevents those thin, delicate slices from falling into the coals.

Brush both sides of your eggplant slices with a neutral oil like avocado or grapeseed oil. Avoid extra virgin olive oil for high-heat grilling as it can smoke too quickly. Place the slices on the mat, leaving a little space between each piece to allow heat to circulate.

Since you are using a mat, you don't have to worry about the eggplant sticking to the metal. Grill for about 3-5 minutes per side. You're looking for a deep golden brown color and a texture that gives slightly when pressed with a spatula.

Seasoning for Maximum Vegan Flavor

Eggplant is like a sponge—it takes on whatever flavors you give it. While a simple pinch of salt and pepper works, I like to elevate my sandwich eggplant with a more robust profile. Try these combinations:

  • Mediterranean: Dried oregano, garlic powder, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice after grilling.
  • Umami Bomb: A light brush of soy sauce and smoked paprika before they hit the grill.
  • Spicy: A dusting of chipotle powder and cumin for a southwest-style sandwich.

Pro tip: Always add fresh herbs or acidic elements (like balsamic glaze or lemon) after the eggplant comes off the grill. This keeps the flavors bright and prevents the sugars in the glazes from burning on the mat.

Building the Perfect Vegan Eggplant Sandwich

Now that you have your perfectly grilled slices, the assembly is where the magic happens. Because grilled eggplant is soft, you need contrasting textures to make the sandwich satisfying.

Start with a toasted piece of crusty bread. Spread a generous layer of vegan pesto or a garlic-herb aioli on the bottom. Layer on your grilled eggplant slices, then add some fresh baby arugula or spinach for a peppery crunch. To add some tang, I highly recommend adding sun-dried tomatoes or pickled red onions.

If you want a heartier meal, add sliced avocado or a slab of vegan mozzarella. Press the sandwich slightly to meld the flavors together, and you have a gourmet vegan meal that rivals any deli sandwich.

Cleaning Up and Mat Maintenance

One of the best parts of using BBQ Grill Mats is that they save you from scrubbing the grill grates after every session. Once you've finished grilling your eggplant, simply remove the mat from the grill and let it cool.

Depending on how much oil you used, you can usually just wipe the mat down with a damp cloth or wash it with warm, soapy water. Since they are reusable, you can keep them in your kitchen drawer for the next time you want to grill delicate vegetables like zucchini, asparagus, or more eggplant.

FAQ

Do I need to peel the eggplant first?

No, leave the skin on. The skin helps the eggplant hold its shape during the grilling process and provides a nice textural contrast. Most eggplant skins are tender and completely edible once cooked.

Can I grill eggplant slices on mat using a gas or charcoal grill?

Yes, these mats work on both gas and charcoal grills. They provide a consistent heat barrier and prevent flare-ups regardless of your fuel source, making them ideal for any outdoor setup.

What if my eggplant is still tasting bitter?

If you find your eggplant is too bitter, you likely skipped the salting step. Next time, salt the slices for at least 20 minutes and rinse or pat them dry. If the cooked eggplant is bitter, a drizzle of balsamic glaze or a squeeze of lemon can help balance the flavor.
